key_insight: In early ER-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer, the absence of high-risk morphology clusters at the tumour front identifies a lower-risk group beyond the paper’s global AI score.
clinical_relevance: Spatially localizing AI predictions on whole-slide images may improve prognostic stratification and help flag patients whose recurrence risk is underestimated by standard clinicopathologic factors or slide-level scoring alone.
method: Swedish multicentre cohort of 6,106 primary invasive breast cancer patients; 3,078 training and 3,028 independent external test.
Used tile-level high-grade morphology scores from a vision-transformer model (ViT_DG/DeepGrade adaptation).
Defined a binary biomarker based on clusters of high-risk tiles at the invasive tumour front and tested associations with recurrence outcomes using multivariable Cox models.
evidence_signal: In the pre-specified ER-positive/HER2-negative/lymph-node-negative/Grade 1–2 subgroup, tumour-front clusters were seen in 37% of training and 39% of test patients and were linked to about a 2.30-fold higher recurrence risk in the external test set.
watch_item: This biomarker is derived from a specific retrospective multicentre dataset and needs prospective validation and robust slide-scanning/segmentation standardization before routine use.
paper_title: A spatial AI-based biomarker with independent prognostic value in early low- and intermediate- risk breast cancer
